homes.home:
Aven — your coding agent

Projects

  • alpha — alpha
  • beta — beta, beta-infra

How to use me

  • Agents asking agents — an agent configured to send can ask other agents or request work from them, in this installation or another one; the answer arrives in its own thread as quoted data from that agent, and its trail shows when an answer folded into a running turn. When a thread holds another client's data, a message that would carry it elsewhere waits as a ✋ Held card: anyone who may drive the thread can Send it (once) or Dismiss it.

  • Audit asks — /asks lists the recent tasks between agents (held first, with cost), /asks <task id> shows a transcript, /asks cancel <task id> cancels one. (Operators' home workspace only.)

  • Build / collaborate — @-mention me with a task in a project channel. I reply in a thread; keep replying (no need to re-mention) and I remember the conversation.

  • Quick private answer — /<question> in a project channel. I answer privately in our DM.

  • DM me directly — just message me in a DM; if it's not clear which project you mean, I'll show a picker.

  • Schedule a digest — /schedule weekdays 9:00 | what to report posts a recurring read-only summary here; /schedule task weekdays 19:30 | what to do runs a job that may edit and commit as the project's instructions say; manage with /routines (/routines all lists every job across this workspace's projects). Routine results arrive as a thread — reply there to continue with the same context.

  • Share files — drop screenshots, PDFs, or docs into a thread or DM (with or without a note) and I'll read them as part of the task; works in Slack Connect channels too. If I can't use a file, I'll reply saying which one and why. (Voice/video not supported yet.)

  • Jot a note — start a message with ! and I'll stay out of it (no agent run).

  • Stop me — hit ✖ Cancel on any working message.

  • See how I got there — hit 🧭 Show steps on a working message (live) or a finished answer for the tool-by-tool trail in a pop-up; a very long run comes condensed.

  • Background agents — if I kick off a background subagent that's still running when I reply, I'll follow up with a new 🔔 Background update message in the thread once it finishes. (A sandbox nobody is using may be put to sleep after a while; background work still running then ends with it.)

  • Long tasks — if a task runs long I won't cut it off: past ~15 minutes the working message stops ticking and turns into a 🌙 Working in the background card (🧭 Show steps still live, ✖ Cancel still stops me), and the answer arrives as a new message in the thread when it's done.

  • Review a PR — /review <PR url or #number> [low|med|high] posts a read-only review here (works in DMs too). /review auto on|off [effort] reviews new PRs automatically (managed from the project's owner workspace).

  • Watch a PR — /autofix <PR> pings here on CI failures / new reviews with a Fix button (/autofix off <PR> / list).

  • Auto-investigate support tickets — tag a YouTrack ticket with the agreed label and I open a thread in the matching project channel: the ticket card (description, priority, links, files — 🔍 Full ticket pops up the whole thing, comments included) followed by a read-only investigation, then I ping the owners. Reply in that thread to dig deeper (I keep the context) or ask me there to implement the fix and open a pull request, or hit 📝 Report to YouTrack to post an internal comment back to the ticket — a pop-up takes your instructions (a one-liner is fine; fixed delivery rules are always appended), then the draft comes back for review/edit before posting (or tick post immediately to send the answer word-for-word) (pilot; only for projects with a YouTrack mapping above). The card shows who flagged the ticket, and the writeup follows the ticket's own language so support can relay it — except when one of the team's own accounts applies the tag, which gets you the answer in English.

  • What's here — /access shows this channel's repos + tools.

  • Inspect my context — /memory shows what I've learned, with a button per topic to drill in (/memory <topic> also works, /memory live reads the sandbox now, /memory log shows snapshot history); /prompt shows my system prompt.

  • Memory upkeep — /dream on/off schedules (or pauses) nightly memory consolidation; /dream for status, /dream now to run it once.

  • Sandbox upkeep — /housekeeping on/off schedules (or pauses) the nightly janitor (dockerd guard, docker prune when disk runs high, stale-worktree reap); /housekeeping for the last run, /housekeeping now to run it once.

  • Status — /status for a live view of sandboxes, sessions, open PRs — and (operators) the Claude subscription quota, on an installation that runs on a subscription token.

  • Check or restart a thread — hit ⚙️ Session on any finished answer for a private status card (session, repos/tools, running turn, PR) and a 🔄 Restart session control if you want the next message to start a brand-new conversation.

  • Tell me if it landed — every answer carries 👍 Helped / 👎 Missed. One click is enough; the count on the button updates so you see it registered, and a thumbs-down asks what went wrong in a short pop-up. Nothing is posted in the thread; click the other button to change your mind.

  • Usage — /usage [days] for token/cost/turn totals per project (and per routine, for scheduled ones), plus how many answers people rated as helpful and what those cost — per-turn figures, last 30d by default; records from before the per-turn cost fix are listed separately as legacy. (Operators' home workspace only.)

  • Who may drive me — /users shows this workspace's access (everyone, by default); admins can restrict to an allowlist and manage it with allow @user / deny @user / open.

  • Reload config — /reload re-reads the project registry (projects.config.json + projects.d/*.md prompts) without a restart; applies to new sessions. (Operators' home workspace only.)

  • Connected sources — projects with linked mail, chat or calendar archives are pulled every 15 minutes on the bot host and scrubbed before anything reaches me; ask me about a thread or a meeting and I cite the original.

  • Pasted secrets stay here — passwords, tokens, API keys and connection strings in what you type are redacted to [REDACTED:…] before the model sees them (same secret → same tag, so I can still tell them apart). Prefer linking to a vault entry over pasting a credential; if I ask for one, give me a reference, not the value.

Commands are /verb … in any room or private conversation; a top-level post in a room starts a thread, no mention needed.
